[[Category:Random variable| ]]
A '''random variable''' is a [[variable]] whose value is probabilistic.

== Formal definition ==

[[Function]]

$$
X:\Omega\to E,
$$

is a '''random variable''' if

* $\Omega=\{\omega\}$ is the [[set]] of all possible outcomes of a [[random event]], known as the '''sample space''',
* $E=X(\Omega)$ is the [[set]] of all possible values of $X$, known as the '''value space'''.

{{Hidden example}}
Let $\Omega=\mathbb{R}$, then

$$
X(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
1,&\omega\text{ is even},\\
0,&\omega\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

is a '''random variable''' with value space $E=\{0,1\}$.
{{End hidden}}

== Probability ==

For $B \subseteq E$

$$
P(X\in B)=P(\{\omega\in\Omega:X(\omega)\in B\}).
$$
